title: Cleveland Clinic, RIKEN, and IBM Cross 12,000-Atom Barrier in Heterogeneous Quantum-Classical Drug Binding Simulations - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Cleveland Clinic, RIKEN and IBM ran the largest heterogeneous quantum-classical electronic-structure calculation to date, simulating solvated protein-ligand complexes of over 12,000 atoms on two 156-qubit Heron r2 QPUs plus three supercomputers. The campaign delivered the first HQC protein-ligand binding energy prediction and a 210x fragment accuracy gain over prior quantum-embedding methods.

insights.claim: A Cleveland Clinic, RIKEN and IBM Quantum collaboration executed what the article calls the largest heterogeneous quantum-classical electronic-structure calculation to date, simulating full solvated protein-ligand complexes exceeding 12,000 atoms.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Pushes hybrid quantum chemistry toward drug-relevant system sizes, supporting the pharma use-case narrative for IBM.
insights.locator: A research collaboration spanning the Cleveland Clinic

insights.claim: The campaign used two 156-qubit IBM Heron r2 processors (ibm_cleveland and ibm_kobe) with up to 94 active qubits, executing 21,006 circuits over more than 239 QPU hours to gather 3.0 billion measurement shots.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows the substantial QPU time real hybrid workloads consume, relevant to quantum cloud revenue models.

insights.claim: The simulated systems, trypsin-benzamidine (12,635 atoms) and T4-lysozyme-n-butyl-benzene (11,608 atoms), are more than 40x larger than the prior 303-atom Trp-cage benchmark, with up to 31,795 molecular orbitals.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A 40x jump in molecular size in one step indicates rapid methodological progress.

insights.claim: Classical resources included Fugaku (152,064 nodes), Miyabi-G (1,104 GH200 nodes) and ROQUO (126 GB200 nodes), with GPU-accelerated Selected-Basis Diagonalization reaching 72.5% strong-scaling parallel efficiency.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hybrid quantum chemistry is a heavy consumer of leadership-class GPU compute, including GH200/GB200-class nodes.

insights.claim: The researchers' localized Embedded Wavefunction (EWF) formalism partitions macromolecules into spatially bounded atomic neighborhoods, reducing fragment construction cost from cubic O(M3) scaling to constant O(1) scaling per fragment.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Scaling improvements in classical pre-processing are what make larger quantum-assisted simulations tractable.
insights.locator: Accurately predicting how small-molecule drugs bind

insights.claim: TrimSQD, an extension of sample-based quantum diagonalization that filters and merges configurations across GPU subgroups, achieved 0.10 mHa deviation versus DMRG on trypsin's largest 45-orbital fragment, a 210x accuracy gain over ExtSQD.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Accuracy against DMRG is the credibility test for quantum chemistry claims.

insights.claim: Standard density functional theory approximations can misrank drug binding affinities, while full-system wavefunction methods exceed classical memory limits, which is the gap hybrid quantum-classical methods aim to bridge.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Defines the value proposition for quantum in drug discovery: accuracy where DFT fails at scales where exact methods cannot run.
insights.quote: standard density functional theory approximations can misrank binding affinities
insights.locator: Accurately predicting how small-molecule drugs bind

insights.claim: The campaign produced the first heterogeneous quantum-classical protein-ligand binding energy prediction, resolving T4-lysozyme binding affinity at -21.07 kcal/mol using a mixed-basis (3-21G / STO-3G) workflow.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A first binding-energy output moves quantum chemistry closer to an actual pharma deliverable, though at minimal basis sets.

insights.claim: A Prefect-based automated workflow controller orchestrated asynchronous job queues between IBM Quantum Runtime and the ROQUO supercomputer, processing 608 million measurement samples in 62.4 hours of wall-clock time without manual intervention.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Workflow automation is a prerequisite for productized hybrid quantum-HPC services.

insights.claim: The campaign was funded by the U.S. National Science Foundation, the National Institutes of Health, Japan's NEDO and the MEXT Supercomputer Fugaku program.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: US-Japan public funding continues to underwrite quantum-HPC research.
